title: Orbit batch recommender — phased workload fingerprinting and incremental apply
creator: Lena Park
description:
Goal: Deliver a recommender that synthesizes per-workload batching + KV-caching parameters using phase-aware fingerprints and can safely apply deltas via a shadow-and-incremental-apply pipeline. The system should improve tokens/second-cost by at least 8% on tail workloads without increasing P95 latency beyond configured SLOs.

Context: Existing continuous batching experiments show strong median cost wins but are brittle on workloads with multi-modal arrival patterns. We need a safer way to propose and then apply parameter changes (batch_size, max_wait_ms, kv_cache_window, batching_mode) that accounts for temporal phases, warm/cold starts, and multi-tenant isolation.

High-level approach:
1) Fingerprinting: capture lightweight per-workload signatures (interarrival distribution summary, payload token histogram, KV reuse rate, session stickiness, model family). Fingerprints are computed in streaming fashion with bounded memory and TTL.
2) Phase detection: run a rolling clustering over recent fingerprints to extract stable phases (e.g., morning ramp, bursty micro-bursts, low-traffic steady). Each phase has its own candidate parameter set.
3) Heuristics + simulated annealing: for each phase, generate candidate parameter deltas using heuristic rules and a small simulated annealer that optimizes a cost-latency objective derived from sampled traces.
4) Shadow evaluation: before applying, run candidate config in shadow mode on a percentage of traffic inside a dedicated shadow pool and run replayed traces with KV-cache enabled to measure regressed signals.
5) Incremental apply and rollback: if shadow metrics meet thresholds, apply config to a small cohort using canary increments with automated safety checks and automated rollback on signal deviations.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Fingerprint frequency vs. overhead: we use 1-min summaries by default and adaptive sampling for very high qps workloads.
- Shadow pool cost: budget-limited; we will prioritize high-cost/high-savings cohorts.
- Safety-first: default to conservative suggestions; provide PMs/owners a way to opt-in to more aggressive deltas.

Success metrics:
- Overall unit-cost reduction (tokens-per-dollar) on evaluated cohorts >= 8% within 30 days of rollout.
- No more than 1% of cohort changes trigger auto-rollback per month.
- P95 latency regressions across cohorts <= 5% (absolute) compared to baseline.
Acceptance_criteria:
- Fingerprinting pipeline emits stable signatures for 95% of non-ephemeral workloads.
- Phase detector identifies >80% of manual phase labels in a small labeled test set.
- Shadow evaluation produces cost & latency delta estimates accurate within +/-10% of subsequent canary measurements.
- Canary->full rollout pipeline includes automated rollback triggers and runs end-to-end in staging.
- Docs and runbook published; initial dashboard filters available in Console for cohort view.
tasks: Design fingerprint schema and proto (fields, TTL, storage) and record in Confluence
Implement lightweight fingerprint emitter in serving runtime (C++ hot path + metrics export)
Build phase-detection microservice (Python/Go) with streaming clustering and API
Prototype candidate generator and local simulator (notebook + library) for cost-latency scoring
Implement shadow runner integration in routing plane and cost accounting hooks
Create canary orchestration workflow (shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25%) with rollback playbook
Add telemetry dashboards for suggested changes, shadow outcomes, canary results, and rollback events
End-to-end tests in staging with replay harness and synthetic multi-phase workloads
Run a 2-week pilot on two internal high-cost customers before broader rollout
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): deploy fingerprint emitter + phase detector with 24hr rolling retention; run replay harness for 48-72h to validate fingerprints. Phase B (shadow pilot): 2-week shadow on 2 internal cohorts (<=5% traffic per cohort). Phase C (canary): incremental apply 1% -> 5% -> 25% with 24h observation windows and automated rollback checks. Phase D (gradual rollout): expand to additional cohorts prioritized by cost-impact and safety score. Final: document and enable self-serve opt-in in Console.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive batch increases can hurt tail latency. Mitigation: conservative default bounds + mandatory shadow evaluation.
Risk: fingerprint drift during incidents leads to bad suggestions. Mitigation: incident label propagation to pause recommender and require manual review.
Risk: shadow evaluation cost exceeds budget. Mitigation: prioritized cohort selection and simulated replay to reduce expensive shadow time.
Risk: telemetry gaps cause false negatives. Mitigation: add synthetic probes and healthchecks for fingerprint emitter and shadow runner.
